SemanticCache validity key includes a monotonic data_version (PRAGMA data_version) or content hash. ANN fingerprint likewise incorporates the same discriminator. close_reason: Fixed in PR #14/#15/#16/#17. See PR for details + regression tests. Verified on spark (cargo test + clippy).

title: Red-test: duty_cycle_ms quantization vs limit_pct
description:
## Kind
red-test | counterexample

## Claim
`duty_cycle_ms` uses CYCLE_MS=10 and `work_ms = max(1, CYCLE_MS * limit / 100)`, so claimed 1% CPU yields 1ms work / 10ms cycle = 10% work fraction. Values outside [1,80] for ASGREP_CPU_LIMIT_PERCENT silently fall back to 80 via parse_cpu_limit.

## Evidence (packet)
- crates/ast-sgrep-cli/src/supervisor.rs:39-46 duty_cycle_ms
- crates/ast-sgrep-cli/src/supervisor.rs:32-37 parse_cpu_limit
- .math-review/runs/20260716T044857Z-ast-sgrep/passes/pass-01/evidence/symbol_pollution_probe.json
- state model PASS: passes/pass-01/evidence/state_supervisor_duty.out.json

## Acceptance (optimizer)
- [ ] Unit tests: for limit in {1,10,50,80}, assert work+sleep==10 and work==max(1,(10*limit)//100)
- [ ] Document that effective floor is 10% of cycle at 1% setting OR increase CYCLE_MS for finer granularity
- [ ] parse_cpu_limit(\"100\") and \"0\" behavior documented or rejected with error (product decision)
- [ ] cargo test -p ast-sgrep-cli supervisor (or new module tests) pass
- [ ] br close only when tests green

## Out of scope
Windows non-Unix supervisor path; rewriting SIGSTOP policy.
close_reason: Added quantization and invalid-range unit tests plus explicit effective-floor/default docs; cargo test -p ast-sgrep-cli supervisor --lib passed 2/2; commit fc27ad2

title: AgentCapsule recalculates prevented_read_bytes ≠ SearchResponse field
description:
## Kind
counterexample / format invariant

## Claim
`to_agent_capsule_json` must preserve or document `SearchResponse.prevented_read_bytes` semantics; agent format passes through core field while capsule redefines it.

## Evidence (ua-surfaces)
- `crates/ast-sgrep-plugins/src/lib.rs:149-162` agent: uses `response.prevented_read_bytes`
- `crates/ast-sgrep-plugins/src/lib.rs:186-204` capsule: `returned_excerpt_bytes` recomputed from previews/excerpts; `prevented_read_bytes = read_bytes_estimate.saturating_sub(returned_excerpt_bytes)`
- When `excerpt_lines==0`, returned bytes ≈ preview lengths, so prevented_read_bytes inflates vs agent path on same response

## Red-test
Fixed `SearchResponse` with nonzero `prevented_read_bytes` and multi-line excerpts:
- assert agent JSON field equals core value
- assert capsule either equals core OR documents formula in schema; fail if silent redefinition differs by >0

title: Multi-station Jackson: watch debounce→update_paths→sidecars→duty search

title: cap_per_file diversity may demote global top-k (document or test)
description:
## Kind
red-test | measurement-gap

## Claim
Hybrid finish_response sorts by score then `cap_per_file` keeps first MAX_HITS_PER_FILE=3 per file and appends overflow at end before `hits.truncate(limit)`. A 4th hit in one file with score above other files' lower hits can fall outside limit. This is diversity bias, not pure score top-k.

## Evidence (packet)
- crates/ast-sgrep-core/src/search/mod.rs:24 MAX_HITS_PER_FILE
- crates/ast-sgrep-core/src/search/mod.rs:268-281 hybrid sort + cap + truncate
- crates/ast-sgrep-core/src/search/mod.rs:380-394 cap_per_file

## Acceptance (optimizer)

- [ ] Document contract in search API docs OR make cap optional
- [ ] cargo test -p ast-sgrep-core search

## Out of scope
Changing default diversity without product sign-off.

title: LSP request path: stdio+index_lock M/G/1 HOL blocks under bg index (Kingman/PK FAIL)
description:
## Kind
performance-law | queue / latency

## Claim
Editor-facing LSP latency is not free-parallel. Single-threaded stdio (`server.rs:39-52`) plus global `index_lock` (`backend.rs:79-105`) serializes all locked index/search work. Background `index_all` holds the mutex for long wall time (`backend.rs:115-125`), producing head-of-line blocking. Kingman/PK cases with high service CV fail claimed mean-wait budgets.

- Notes: `request_path_notes.md`

## Distinct from
- **5du.25**: unbounded single-waiter mutex timeout (liveness/speculative)
- **jk7.9 / 5du.38**: duty-cycle / watch multi-station (CLI), not LSP request path

## Acceptance
- [ ] Document LSP blocking semantics (progress / partial results)
- [ ] Measure p99 lock-hold during index_all under load
- [ ] Optional: try_lock + deferred work or separate read path

## Related

title: FP gate: MIN_SIMILARITY membership not scale-invariant under query scale (product-dot)
description:
## Kind

## Claim

## Evidence

- Related: `jk7.2`, `5du.16`

## Acceptance
- [ ] Gate uses true cosine OR both sides L2-normalized before thr OR document magnitude coupling
- [ ] Re-run probe: product membership stable under query scale OR thr applied post-normalize

## Labels
counterexample, math-review, pass-16, numerical-fp
close_reason: Implemented true L2-normalized cosine similarity with f64 accumulation; positive query scaling no longer changes threshold membership. Static evidence: cosine divides dot by both vector norms; zero norms return 0.

title: EPIC: Fusion retrieval — sub-1ms lexical+AST+semantic hybrid
SIMD literal prefilter + Amdahl profiling of serial fraction
description: memchr/aho-corasick/trigram prefilter so non-candidate files are never parsed. Profile parse->match->rank with work-span methodology (T1, T_inf, Brent bound — promoted from math-review 5du.37): measure serial fraction rigorously BEFORE any N-core speedup work, attack largest serial term. Work-stealing parallelism across files; incremental reparse. Also subsumes 5du.35 break-even arithmetic (4.6% embed / 3.0% sqlite): e2hc.11 content-hash cache dwarfs those targets; re-derive break-evens after profiling.
close_reason: Completed on PR 21 in commit 2640392. Native pattern search now uses SIMD memmem to reject noncandidate files before UTF8 conversion or parsing, Rayon work stealing for candidate files, and deterministic result ordering while preserving the indexed signature fast path. Added exact hit identity comparison across no prefilter, one worker prefiltered, and production parallel runs. Five repeated release perf samples show 71 percent file rejection, 3.02 times prefilter speedup, and 0.163 percent median serial fraction with honest T1, T infinity, Brent, and scheduler overhead accounting. Targeted Spark tests passed four of four, parity passed five of five, clippy passed, three Jeffrey adversarial passes completed, and an independent verifier passed.

title: Vector quantization: int8 + binary/Hamming prefilter with f32 rescore
description: Embed crate stores full f32. Add int8 scalar quantization (4x) and optional binary sign quantization with Hamming prefilter + exact rescore of top candidates (32x scan reduction). Smaller index, fewer touched pages (compounds with mmap bead), faster IVF scan, lower RAM ceiling for e2hc.8 rlimit. Recall regression gate in bench_suite: <1% recall@10 loss vs f32 baseline.

title: Content-hash embedding cache: never re-embed unchanged code

Critical for cloud embed path (ASGREP_EMBED_API_KEY -> paid API): unchanged code must cost $0. Cache lives in .asgrep/, versioned by embedder model id.

title: Query result cache keyed by (query, index fingerprint)
description: Agents re-run near-identical queries constantly. Cache final ranked results keyed by normalized query + index fingerprint (fingerprints already in store/sqlite.rs); any index patch changes fingerprint -> sound invalidation for free. Repeat queries return in microseconds. Bounded size, LRU, lives in .asgrep/.

title: Hash embedding uses 32 of 256 sign bits: all vectors live in 32-dim subspace
description: omega-math pass-1 #16 (CRITICAL). semantic.rs:143-152: sign bit is bytes[i % 32] & 1 — pattern repeats with period 32 across the 256 slots, so every embedding is a 32-bit sign pattern tiled 8x. Effective dimension 32, not 256; feature crosstalk ~2.8x worse than designed; cross-doc noise floor ~1/sqrt(32)=0.177 EXCEEDS MIN_SIMILARITY=0.08, so the threshold does not clear the noise floor of the backend it guards (math.rs:6). blake3 digest has 256 bits — one independent bit per slot available and unused. Fix: (bytes[i/8] >> (i%8)) & 1; bump backend version to force reindex; then re-derive MIN_SIMILARITY. Evidence: .pi-subagents/artifacts/52b04417_reviewer_0_output.md
close_reason: Fixed in PR #14/#15/#16/#17. See PR for details + regression tests. Verified on spark (cargo test + clippy).

title: Fusion normalization unsound: term-count ceilings dilute; lexical capped at 1/terms; single-char queries zeroed
description: omega-math pass-1 #7/#8 + pass-2 #30 (MAJOR). (a) intent.rs:155-195 channel_ceiling scales linearly with query term count, re-diluting scores by unmatched terms — defeats the anti-dilution invariant documented at rank.rs:77-79 and tested at rank.rs:143-155 (test only covers pre-normalization value). (b) passes/lexical.rs:66-80 issues ONE OR-query so ranks vec always has length 1 and fuse_rrf never fuses; max raw lexical = rrf(0)*200≈3.279 while ceiling = terms*3.279 — normalized lexical hard-capped at 1/terms, so noise-floor embed hits and binary Graph hits (1.0*weight) structurally outrank perfect lexical matches on multi-term queries. (c) intent.rs:180-182 substantive_terms requires >1 char — exact single-char symbol queries (i, x) are zeroed at routing, contradicting tested invariant rank.rs:101-107. Fix direction: normalize by matched-term count or per-hit achievable max; term-count-free Asgrep ceiling OR genuine per-term FTS fusion; treat exact single-char matches as substantive. Blocks e2hc.4 (fusion ranker must not inherit this). Evidence: both reviewer artifacts.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #22. Asgrep ceiling term-count multiplier removed; single-char substantive_terms filter fixed. 3 regression tests. Reviewed by worker subagent: fix sound, no P0/P1. P2 follow-up (Def/Caller dilution) filed as u9fj. P3 (per-term FTS fusion) deferred.

title: Signal provenance + margins on every hit (rigor tiering)
description: Every hit carries (signal: exact|structural|semantic, score, margin). Fusion never lets a fuzzy semantic score masquerade as an exact match — tiered like ITB rigor tags. JSON output surfaces per-signal provenance for agents.
close_reason: Completed on PR 21 in commit 77232c2. Every hit now carries kind derived signal provenance, score, and a finite within signal margin. Semantic evidence cannot spoof exact provenance through construction or legacy JSON decode. Margins are computed after deduplication and file filtering, ties and terminal candidates return zero, and extreme finite differences saturate at the finite maximum. Native, GitHub, GitLab, agent, capsule, CLI, MCP, and LSP JSON retain the fields. Targeted DGX Spark tests passed core five, plugins three, LSP three, and CLI two. Four package clippy passed. Three initial plus two post fix Jeffrey adversarial passes completed. Independent full surface verification passed.

title: Fix spherical k-means seed distance: use nearest-centroid distance (1 - max cosine)
description: omega-math pass-5 #89 (MINOR, high leverage for ANN quality). semantic_ann.rs:286-295 chooses farthest-point seeds using 1 - min(cosine(v,c)); distance to the NEAREST existing centroid is 1 - max(cosine(v,c)). After the second centroid, a vector identical to one centroid but opposite another can be selected again, creating duplicate/dead seeds and weaker partitions. Fix seed metric; add adversarial unit test with duplicate/opposite vectors. Pair with e2hc.19: ANN recall tests must run n>=2000 or thread the effective threshold so this path is actually exercised.

title: HNSW graph ANN index: log(n) semantic search at 100k+ symbols
description: Current ANN is IVF-flat (semantic_ann.rs): candidate_indices probes sqrt(k) clusters then brute-force cosine over members. Complexity ~O(n/k * probes) — at 100k symbols with 256 clusters, probe scan still touches ~hundreds of vectors. HNSW (hierarchical navigable small world) gives O(log n) search with efSearch tuning, sub-ms p99 at 100k+ with recall@10 >= 0.95 at ef=64. Replace or complement .asgrep/semantic.ivf with .asgrep/semantic.hnsw (versioned MAGIC header preserved, same fingerprint invalidation). Build at index time (slower build, faster query — acceptable trade for sub-1ms). Acceptance: bench_suite semantic p99 < 1ms at 10k symbols, < 5ms at 100k; recall@10 >= 0.95 vs brute-force baseline; memory ceiling documented; regression test vs existing IVF. Compounds with e2hc.10 (quantization) and e2hc.9 (mmap).

title: Native structural pattern matcher: kill ast-grep subprocess fallback
description: pattern.rs:35 search_pattern_ast_grep spawns external ast-grep binary for any pattern needs_ast_grep_fallback() — measured 2.1s p50 vs ast-grep native 34ms (speed.md ripgrep corpus, struct RegexMatcherBuilder). The subprocess is THE dominant structural-mode loss. Implement in-process tree-sitter structural matcher using ast-sgrep-lang PatternNode signatures already extracted at index time: support metavariables ($NAME, $$$), kind predicates, deep equality over pattern_nodes table + re-parse only on miss. Target: zero subprocess spawns for the 29-pattern bake-off suite; p50 < 50ms at 23k files for any pattern. Acceptance: parity test passes for all 29 bake-off patterns without ast-grep binary installed; speed.md structural row improves on ripgrep/flask/self; documented patterns that still require fallback (if any) listed. Blocks e2hc.5 scorecard.
close_reason: Removed the production ast-grep subprocess fallback. Structural search now uses exact indexed signatures and native tree-sitter matching for declarations, kind predicates, calls, and metavariables, with unsupported nested rules documented explicitly. All 29 fixed bakeoff patterns resolved without ast-grep. A release RCH probe over 23,001 indexed files measured 0.00375 millisecond p50 across 101 samples versus the 50 millisecond ceiling. Targeted language, core, parity, latency, and clippy checks passed. Commit d0162c9 pushed to pull request 21.

title: Aho-Corasick multi-needle literal prefilter: single-pass N-term scan
description: Hybrid queries with N terms run N separate literal_pass/trigram lookups (search/mod.rs run_serial_passes loops passes per term). For 3-5 term NL queries this is 3-5x SQLite trigram + BMH scans. Build an Aho-Corasick automaton over all query terms (memchr crate or vendors/aho-corasick) and run a single streaming scan over lines_trigram candidate rows, emitting per-term hits with term-id provenance. Eliminates redundant line reads and SQLite round-trips. Acceptance: bench_suite multi-term literal p50 >= 2x faster vs N=4 baseline on 23k corpus; term-id attribution preserved into fusion (channel scores unchanged); single-term path unchanged (no regression). Compounds with e2hc.1 SIMD prefilter.

title: GPU/BLAS GEMV embedding backend: cuBLAS + Apple Metal/MPS for batched cosine
description: Current top_k_flat_similarity (math.rs:80) uses simsimd f32::dot per vector, rayon parallel at PARALLEL_CHUNK_THRESHOLD=64. At 100k x 256-dim this is 25.6M MACs/query — fits BLAS sgemv (single query x matrix) at <100us on any modern GPU/CPU-BLAS. Add optional BLAS backend: Apple Accelerate vecLib sgemv (macOS, always-on via metal feature), Intel MKL/oneAPI on x86_64, cuBLAS on CUDA hosts. Fallback to simsimd when unavailable. Quantized path (e2hc.10) covers CPU scan; this covers f32 rescore + large-batch IVF/HNSW. Acceptance: optional feature flag blas; bench_suite semantic p50 >= 5x faster at 100k symbols when enabled; zero regression when disabled; CI runs disabled path. Compounds with e2hc.21 HNSW.

title: Early-termination fusion with confidence bound: stop passes when top-k decisive
description: search_hybrid runs all passes (lexical/symbol/anchor/structural/embed) to completion, then fuses. For high-confidence literal queries the embed pass is wasted work; for high-similarity embed hits the lexical+symbol passes are redundant. Add a confidence-gated cascade: after each pass, compute top-k margin (score_1 - score_k) and channel coverage; if margin exceeds threshold AND >= k hits at SCORE_* bound, skip remaining passes. Preserves worst-case recall via fallback-to-all-passes when margin low. Distinct from e2hc.3 cascade planner (which is about lexical->AST->semantic ordering); this is about per-pass early-exit within a chosen order. Acceptance: bench_suite hybrid p50 >= 30% faster on literal-dominant queries; zero MRR regression on bake-off gold set; threshold tuned by measurement not guessed; documented worst-case (low-margin) latency unchanged.

title: Optional in-process daemon mode: Unix-socket pre-warmed Searcher
description: e2hc.8 mandates zero-resident (NO daemon ever) — correct default for safety/CI. But interactive LSP/agent loops pay process spawn + SQLite open + IVF mmap on every call (~10ms CLI startup floor). Add OPTIONAL asgrep-daemon: Unix domain socket at .asgrep/daemon.sock, pre-warmed Searcher with semantic cache + mmap IVF hot, request/response = serde JSON over length-prefixed frames. Single-shot asgrep auto-spawns daemon if ASGREP_DAEMON=1 and reuses; falls back to in-process if socket stale. This is the inverse bet to e2hc.8: e2hc.8 wins on safety/CI, this wins on interactive p99. Acceptance: asgrep --daemon semantic p99 < 300us at 23k files; --no-daemon unchanged; socket cleanup on SIGTERM/SIGKILL tested; documented as opt-in only, default remains zero-resident.

title: Columnar in-memory symbol/graph cache: zero-SQL hot path for defs/callers/imports
description: Every symbol_pass/anchor_pass/search_callers/search_defs/search_imports issues a fresh SQLite SELECT (store/sqlite.rs calls_matching, SYM_LOC, IMPORT_SELECT). At sub-1ms budget, SQLite round-trips + row materialization dominate. Build an in-memory columnar snapshot (arrow-rs or hand-rolled SoA: name_offsets, file_ids, line_starts, line_ends, kind_codes, caller/callee edge CSR) loaded once per Searcher, invalidated by index_gen bump (existing response_cache mechanism). Symbol lookup becomes binary search over sorted names; graph BFS becomes CSR traversal. Acceptance: defs:/callers: p50 < 200us at 23k symbols; memory ceiling documented (target < 8MB for 100k symbols); SQLite path retained as fallback; parity test passes (ast-sgrep-55hl graph oracle). Compounds with e2hc.9 mmap.

title: Parallel parse fan-out: tree-sitter parsers across N cores at index time
description: index.rs uses rayon par_iter for extraction (line uses rayon prelude) but prl3.1 only tracks DB write concurrency vs parse/prep. Confirm/extend: tree-sitter Parser is !Sync per instance (TSParser opaque), so per-task parser pool from ParserRegistry is needed; benchmark whether parse or SQLite write is the true serial fraction on 23k/100k corpora. If parse-bound, scale parser pool to rayon thread count; if write-bound, defer to prl3.1. Acceptance: cargo bench index cold-build p50 >= 1.5x faster on 8+ core machine vs single-thread baseline; Amdahl serial fraction measured and documented; no parser-registry race (TSParser drop semantics). Sets cold-index floor for sub-1ms warm path.

title: Keystone: single-pass arena fusion — AST+semantic+grep fused top-k under 1ms wall
description:
SUB-1MS FUSION CONTRACT. The fusion STEP itself (not passes) must be <1ms wall at 100k symbols + 23k files. Current finish_response + dedup_hits + cap_per_file + sort + intent::route_hits cannot hold that budget: dedup_hits (types.rs:285) builds a std::HashMap keyed by a 6-tuple of Strings (kind, file, line_start, line_end, symbol, caller, callee) → SipHash over owned Strings per hit + per-hit allocs; cap_per_file sorts then groups; final sort is full O(N log N) total_cmp; route_hits re-walks; estimate_prevented_reads (mod.rs:~565) does a sync fs::metadata syscall per unique file. This bead owns the rewrite to make fusion itself sub-ms so the index+parallel passes (e2hc.21/22/23/27) are not wasted in the merge step.

ARCHITECTURE (single-pass arena fusion):
1. Interned file/symbol/caller/callee IDs (u32 via string interner) — zero String keys in hot path; (file_id, line, kind) packs into u64 dedup key.
2. Per-pass arenas: each pass writes (file_id, line_start, line_end, kind, score, span_id) into its own slab; no intermediate Vec<SearchHit> allocation; passes publish atomically.
3. FxHashSet/FxHashMap for dedup (trusted local index, no SipHash DoS tax) OR robin-hood open addressing with packed u64 keys.
4. partial_sort_top_k via select_nth_unstable_by + truncate — O(N) for top-k instead of O(N log N) full sort; k = options.limit (default 50).
5. Late materialization: SearchHit strings built ONLY for the final top-k, after fusion+sort; cold file paths/symbols/excerpts stay in columnar interned form until the very end.
6. estimate_prevented_reads gated behind --ledger flag (default off); eliminates fs::metadata syscalls from the critical path.
7. cap_per_file replaced by a per-file counter during the single pass (O(N), no prior sort).

BUDGET (target p99, 100k symbols + 23k files, hybrid mode):
- dedup: <200us (FxHashMap + packed u64 keys, ~250 hits)
- top-k partial sort: <50us (select_nth on ~250)
- route_hits: <50us (single pass, no alloc)
- late materialization: <200us (50 hits × string build)
- intent classify: <20us (cached on ParsedQuery)
- TOTAL fusion step: <520us p99, leaves ~480us headroom under 1ms for pass execution

ACCEPTANCE:
- bench_suite fusion-only microbench: <1ms p99 at 250 input hits, <300us p50; reported as 'fusion_step_ms' alongside 'search_total_ms'.
- Zero String-key HashMap in fusion hot path (audit grep on finish_response tree).
- estimate_prevented_reads behind opt-in flag; default path zero syscalls.
- MRR parity with current fusion on bake-off gold set (no ranking change, only mechanism change).
- e2hc.4 (RRF/learned fusion) and e2hc.14 (normalization bug) preserved; arena fusion is the substrate those strategies run on.
- Documentation: this is the bead that makes 'ast-sgrep = AST + semantic + grep fused sub-1ms = fastest framework in the world' a true measured claim rather than marketing.

COORDINATION:
- Substrate for e2hc.4 (learned weights run on arena scores, not SearchHit structs).
- Required-by e2hc.5 scorecard (sub-1ms claim must include fusion step measurement, not just pass execution).
- Pairs with e2hc.25 early-termination (early-exit reads arena state, no separate fusion pass).
- Pairs with e2hc.27 columnar cache (intermed file_id/symbol_id from columnar snapshot, zero copy into arena).

title: Cascade query planner: lexical -> AST -> semantic single-pass pipeline
description: Constraint-cascade (ITB concept): each stage only sees survivors of the previous. Stage 1 literal/trigram prefilter shrinks file set; stage 2 tree-sitter structural match on candidates only; stage 3 semantic rerank on matches only. One query API, one pass.
close_reason: Completed on PR 21 in commit 6222373. Unprefixed queries now run a strict literal or trigram, AST derived structural, then semantic constraint cascade. Stage one handles case folded short and multi term queries and bounds the union to 100 files. Structural SQL applies survivor paths before ceilings. Semantic ranking loads only modern or legacy vectors in structural survivor files. Empty stages stop. Atomic index generations keep response and semantic caches fresh for local and external writes. Targeted DGX Spark verification passed cascade 2, ranking 1, parity 5, provenance 5, semantic cache 1, trigram append 1, and three focused unit gates. Core tests clippy passed with warnings denied. Jeffrey adversarial runs completed three passes plus two final stage one passes. Independent verification converged with no open findings.

title: RRF/learned fusion ranker + weight-sensitivity analysis
description: RRF baseline, then learned weights. Fisher-style sensitivity (ITB stiff-vs-sloppy concept): find which fusion weights actually move rankings so we only tune those.
close_reason: Completed on PR 21 in commit c402425. Hybrid survivors now use weighted reciprocal rank fusion across eight evidence channels. Same channel duplicates do not consume positions, each file and start line emits one deterministic canonical hit, and sorted contributors preserve all positive producer provenance without resurrecting suppressed evidence. Public judged examples support bounded pairwise weight learning. Fisher style sensitivity reports gradient, valid central or boundary curvature, rank churn, and stiffness, and only stiff channels are tuned to local convergence. Learned intent specs deploy through the existing environment contract. All targeted verification ran remotely on the DGX Spark through RCH. Fusion 5, ranking 1, cascade 2, provenance 5, plugin 3, LSP 1, parity 5, semantic cache 1, trigram 1, and three cascade units passed. Three package clippy passed with warnings denied. Three Jeffrey adversarial passes and independent verification converged with no open findings.

title: Benchmark scorecard: sub-1ms budget, honest negatives, vs ast-grep/semgrep/ripgrep

title: Competitive head-to-head bench: grep/ack/ag/wildgrep/hypergrep + ripgrep/semgrep/ast-grep

Extend harness to include BSD grep, GNU grep, ack, ag (silver-searcher), wildgrep, hypergrep, ripgrep-all where installable. Same methodology as speed-headtohead: hyperfine warmup 3 min-runs 10, p50/p95 from raw times, peak RSS one representative run. Corpora: self, ripgrep 14.1.1, flask 3.0.3, plus a 100k corpus per ast-sgrep-59g. Acceptance: results/head-to-head.md extended with new comparator columns; honest losses published (cold scan tools will win on first-query unindexed); one-paragraph physics analysis (index vs scan amortization curve, crossover point).

title: Symbol-level embeddings with parent mapping + max-aggregation scoring (A-RAG)
description: Embed at fine granularity (symbol/AST node, analog of A-RAG sentence embeddings) with mapping back to parent function/file. Parent score = max over child scores; return parent unit with matched children as snippet. Gives fine-grained matching without losing meaningful return units. Touches ast-sgrep-embed semantic.rs.
close_reason: Implemented bounded AST child embeddings mapped to nearest function or file parents, max-aggregated parent scoring, raw matched-child snippets, schema migration, and full backend model identity. Three adversarial passes and targeted Spark tests passed.

title: Agentic end-task eval harness: accuracy + retrieved-tokens + failure taxonomy
description: A-RAG eval methodology on code: agent-loop benchmark where an LLM answers code questions using ast-sgrep tools. Metrics: end-task accuracy, retrieved tokens (context efficiency as first-class metric), steps-to-answer, test-time scaling curve vs max steps. Manual failure taxonomy (entity confusion / wrong strategy / gave up / corpus missing). Complements micro-latency scorecard e2hc.5.

title: Zero-resident incremental reindex: query-time freshness, burst process, hard deadline
description: NO daemon, ever. Freshness is a property of the query: each asgrep invocation runs a staleness check (mtime + structure fingerprints, store/sqlite.rs) and incrementally patches only changed files inside the query process, then the process exits. Constraints as acceptance criteria: (1) no resident process — single-shot spawn->patch->exit; (2) internal watchdog with hard wall-clock deadline, self-kills on overrun; (3) memory ceiling enforced (rlimit), peak RSS asserted in tests; (4) incremental patch budget p99 < 50ms for small change-sets, measured in bench_suite; (5) process-lifetime telemetry so the no-runaway guarantee is provable, not promised. Secondary trigger: optional git-hook / explicit CI one-shot (asgrep index --changed) with identical constraints. This closes the warm-index gap in the sub-1ms story.

title: Zero-copy mmap index layout: O(touched pages) open, OS page cache as the daemon
description: No-daemon means every query pays process spawn + index open + IVF full-file read (semantic_ivf.rs File::read). Replace with mmap-able zero-copy layout (rkyv/bytemuck-style, versioned MAGIC header preserved): open cost = pages actually touched, OS page cache keeps it warm across burst processes with zero resident footprint. Acceptance: cold open p99 and warm open p99 measured in bench_suite; warm open <1ms on medium repo. Keystone that reconciles no-daemon constraint with sub-1ms claim.
close_reason: Implemented aligned read-only mmap semantic IVF vectors with bounded format validation, safe atomic or deferred cross-platform publication, migration and corruption handling, filtered-search isolation, and mapped memory accounting. Measured cold p99 0.963 ms, fresh-inode p99 0.135 ms, and warm p99 0.037 ms. Three Jeffrey passes, parallel Opus worker audits, targeted RCH tests, and clippy passed.

title: F-11: exceeds_threshold ULP wrong for negative min (P3)
description: math.rs:8-19 f32::from_bits(min.to_bits()-1) is more negative for min<0, not less. Filter becomes too permissive. Latent (MIN_SIM=0.08 positive). Fix: clamp min>=0 or handle explicitly. No code change.
design: math.rs:8-19 uses f32::from_bits(min.to_bits()-1) which moves AWAY from zero for negative min (more negative = more permissive). Fix: for min<0 use from_bits(bits+1) direction, or clamp. Latent today because MIN_SIMILARITY=0.08>0; fix to prevent future negative thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: exceeds_threshold handles negative min correctly: the ULP nudge makes the bound strictly less permissive as intended for all sign values, or min is clamped >=0 with a documented rationale. Unit test covers min<0, min=0, min>0 boundaries.
close_reason: Invalid report: negative f32 bit ordering was reversed in the finding; min.to_bits() - 1 is next-up toward zero. Regression test math::contract_tests::exceeds_threshold_negative_min passes on the existing implementation.

title: Watch debounce has no max-latency bound: sustained events starve indexing forever
description: omega-math pass-3 #54 (MAJOR liveness). crates/ast-sgrep-cli/src/lib.rs:722-767: rx.recv_timeout(debounce) is quiet-gap coalescing — timer resets on every event, so an event stream faster than debounce means Timeout never fires: pending grows unbounded and no indexing happens. Index lives under watched root so each update emits fresh events extending the next wait. Fix: track first-pending timestamp, force flush when now-first_pending > k*debounce; consider filtering .asgrep/ self-events. Relevant to e2hc.8 zero-resident reindex (same freshness pipeline).

title: pi runtime: ensureFresh starvation, pending double-count/leak, empty-index reindex loop
description: omega-math pass-3 #63-#65 (minors, one surface). extension/src/runtime.ts: (a) 270-273 ensureFresh waiter is unbounded retry — under sustained writes search before() defers indefinitely (starvation, not deadlock; inFlight cleanup verified sound). Fix: bound retries, serve marginally-stale after N cycles. (b) 242-248+265-269: markAffectedPath bumps dirtyGeneration AND leaves path in #pendingPaths — next ensureFresh double-counts (spurious refresh); out-of-root paths accumulate forever. (c) 191-202+296-302: empty project maps to missing -> full reindex on EVERY search; treat successfully-built empty index as ready. Also #55 supervisor.rs: parse_cpu_limit maps 0 to DEFAULT 80 (operator asks min gets max) + 1-9% all quantize to 10%. title: callers:/imports: return 0 hits despite indexed graph (Issue #12)
description:
Bug: asgrep callers:symbol and imports:symbol return 0 hits even when asgrep status reports caller_count=144959 and import_count=10327.

Reproduction (from issue):
- Indexed pi-mono/senpi TS monorepo, 3,486 files; reindex; doctor reports healthy
- defs:refreshToken returns 5 hits
- callers:refreshToken returns 0 hits
- chain refreshToken returns 345 nodes including CalledBy edges
- pattern/literal/word modes work

Coverage gap observation: callers:/imports: fail for refreshToken, refreshAnthropicToken, refreshOAuthToken, constructor, toString, FileFinder; succeed for main, render, parse.

Suspected root cause: divergent-normalization between indexer write path (stores one symbol form) and callers/imports retrieval pass (queries with a different symbol form). Pattern: data IS indexed and traversable by chain, but not retrievable.

SCOPE (read-only first): investigate, no fixes yet.

Acceptance: identification of exact normalization divergence + minimal repro + fix proposal (separate beads).
design: This is the umbrella Issue #12. It is resolved by the F-01 root-cause fix (powt) plus the normalization investigation (7uz6). Validate against the real 3486-file monorepo counts, not just synthetic fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: callers:symbol and imports:symbol return hit counts consistent with status caller_count=144959 / import_count=10327 on the pi-mono TS fixture, for both lowercase and mixed-case symbols. defs/callers/imports/chain agree on the same symbol set. Regression test added. Closed only after powt lands and the parity oracle (55hl) passes.
notes: INVESTIGATION COMPLETE (PR #18): callers: uses exact_eq_filter (lower()=lower(), case-insensitive); imports: uses like_terms_filter (SQLite LIKE, ASCII case-insensitive). Existing parity test covers callers:RefreshToken case variants. Added imports_mode_is_case_insensitive_on_mixed_case_module_path to close imports: coverage gap. Both pass on spark. Mixed-case 0-hits bug appears already fixed by F-01/z47q. If TS monorepo repro still fails, divergence is NOT case-sensitivity but qualified-callee storage — file separate bead with real corpus.
close_reason: Completed on PR 21 in commits 78b5c3d and e9773b4. Reindexed the real senpi monorepo snapshot on DGX Spark with 3746 files, 22861 symbols, 184409 caller edges, and 12898 imports. The real corpus oracle verified refreshToken definitions, case equivalent caller results, and chain traversal plus additional caller and import keys. Added pinned validation evidence and a CI discovered graph retrieval oracle across four languages and naming styles. Targeted Spark parity tests passed six of six, graph oracle passed one of one, both clippy gates passed, and two independent reviews passed.

title: Implement deterministic index freshness and concurrency

title: F-01: prefixed_mode_query bypasses term lowercasing — callers:/defs:/imports: 0 hits on mixed-case (P0)
description: Root cause of Issue #12. ParsedQuery::parse lowercases via tokenize_for_scoring, but prefixed_mode_query (search/passes/symbol.rs:184-191) overwrites terms with vec![lookup_symbol()] which preserves target case. rank.rs:30-37 normalizes only the symbol side, not the term. score_normalized_symbol: "foo" == "Foo" -> false → score 0 → caller_rows_to_hits drops all rows. Affects LSP goto_definition and find_references too. chain works because calls_matching SQL uses lower() = lower(). Do NOT fix yet — read-only next step is to confirm with minimal repro.
design: Two candidate fix surfaces: (a) prefixed_mode_query builds terms via lookup_symbol().to_lowercase(); (b) score_normalized_symbol / normalized_symbol in rank.rs normalizes BOTH sides. Prefer (b): single normalization chokepoint so LSP (F-04/nuli) and chain inherit the fix automatically and no query path can regress. Keep tokenize_for_scoring semantics; do not change the lowercase-only fast path in normalized_symbol, extend it to the term argument.
acceptance_criteria: Minimal failing repro committed: on a mixed-case fixture, callers:RefreshToken and defs:RefreshToken return 0 while chain returns CalledBy edges (reproduces Issue #12). Root cause confirmed at search/passes/symbol.rs prefixed_mode_query. Fix makes symbol scoring case-insensitive on BOTH term and symbol sides at one chokepoint. After fix: callers:/defs:/imports: return non-zero on mixed-case AND lowercase symbols; rank ordering unit tests unchanged; chain parity preserved; new unit test asserts score_normalized_symbol(RefreshToken, refreshtoken) > 0; integration test green.

title: AST pipeline performance: reduce serial fractions (Amdahl) and remove threshold discontinuities
description: Umbrella for AST/search pipeline performance. Framing: (1) Amdahl's Law — identify and shrink the serial fraction of each hot path so added cores actually help; (2) remove hard threshold cliffs (the file_count>=128 bifurcation, the ANN=2000 cliff) in favor of continuous cost-model scaling; (3) an invertibility invariant that guarantees everything indexed stays retrievable (generalization of Issue #12). Children hold the concrete measured work. All require a reproducible benchmark (crates/ast-sgrep-core/src/bench_suite.rs) before/after.
design: Establish a stable benchmark harness first; attribute measured share of total time per stage so Amdahl bounds are real, not assumed.
acceptance_criteria: Each child is closed only with a before/after benchmark on a fixed corpus (wall time, peak RSS, and for search p50/p95 latency). No speculative optimization without a measured hot path.

title: PERF: pipeline index_all DB writes concurrently with parse/prep (Amdahl serial-fraction cut)
description: index.rs index_all parallelizes file prep via rayon par_iter (prepare_file), then writes the SQLite store SEQUENTIALLY inside one begin_bulk_tx/commit_bulk_tx loop. The write loop is the serial fraction: by Amdahl, if writes are a share S of total time, max speedup is bounded by 1/S regardless of cores. Overlap prep and write so the CPU parses the next batch while a writer thread drains committed rows.
design: Producer/consumer: rayon prep stage feeds a bounded channel; a single writer thread owns the SQLite connection and the bulk transaction (SQLite writers are single-threaded). Batch upserts (e.g. 256 files) to amortize tx overhead; consider WAL + synchronous=NORMAL. Keep prune_missing_files after the drain.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark index_all on a fixed multi-thousand-file corpus before/after. After: wall-clock improves and the sequential write phase no longer dominates; row counts and content hashes are byte-identical to the current serial path; crash/rollback semantics preserved (partial batch still rolls back).

title: PERF: parallelize IVF kmeans assignment step (semantic_ann.rs)
description: semantic_ann.rs kmeans runs 12 iterations; each iteration reassigns every vector to its nearest centroid in a sequential loop (O(n*k*dim)) then recomputes centroids sequentially. For large corpora the assignment loop is the serial hot spot of IVF build. Parallelize assignment with rayon (par_iter over vectors) and reduce centroid sums in parallel.
design: Assignment is embarrassingly parallel: par_iter vectors -> nearest_centroid. Centroid recompute: parallel fold into per-thread sum/count then merge. Keep farthest-point seeding sequential (cheap). Guard determinism by stable reduction order or accept tolerance validated by recall.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark IVF build on a large embedded corpus before/after. After: build wall-time drops with core count; final assignment is deterministic-equivalent given the same seed (or within tolerance); ANN recall unchanged on a fixed query set.

title: PERF: replace hard file_count>=128 search bifurcation with continuous cost-model (Mobius continuum)
description: search/mod.rs bifurcates at PARALLEL_PASS_FILE_THRESHOLD=128: below it passes run serially; at/above it search_hybrid_large spawns 4 thread::scope workers each opening its own IndexStore. This is a discontinuity: 127 vs 129 files take very different paths and the 4-worker fan-out has fixed cost that can lose on medium inputs. Replace the boolean cliff with one continuous decision (Mobius framing: a single continuous surface) that scales worker count by estimated cost (corpus size, enabled passes, embed on/off).
design: Model per-pass cost from store.status (file_count, symbol/caller counts) and options (use_embed, use_rerank). worker_count = clamp(estimated_parallel_work / per_thread_overhead). Reuse a connection pool instead of opening a fresh IndexStore per worker to cut fan-out fixed cost. Fall back to serial when estimated work < overhead.
acceptance_criteria: Microbenchmark across corpus sizes spanning the old threshold (32,64,128,256,1024 files) before/after. After: no latency regression on either side of the old 128 boundary; medium corpora do not pay unnecessary thread/store-open overhead; worst case never slower than today; identical hits to current code.

title: PERF: IVF candidate_indices selects top probes via select_nth instead of full centroid sort
description: semantic_ann.rs candidate_indices sorts ALL centroids by similarity (O(k log k)) then takes the top take (adaptive sqrt(k)). Only the top take are needed so partial selection (select_nth_unstable) is O(k). Small but on the hot query path for every ANN search.
design: Replace full sort with select_nth_unstable_by at index take-1 then iterate the top slice. Members are subsequently sorted/unique anyway. Low-risk; included because it is on every semantic query.
acceptance_criteria: Microbenchmark candidate selection for k in 16..256 before/after. After: fewer comparisons, identical candidate set membership (order within probes irrelevant since members are re-scored and sorted downstream); ANN recall unchanged.

title: PERF: batch chain BFS store queries per depth level (chain.rs)
description: chain.rs graph traversal expands nodes with per-node store queries as it walks depth levels, issuing many small SQL round-trips. Batch all expansions at a given depth into a single IN-list query to cut round-trips from O(nodes) to O(depth).
design: Collect the frontier set at each BFS depth, issue one IN-list query (chunked to SQLite variable limits), map results back. Preserve decay_factor scoring and dedup. Coordinate with z47q (case-insensitive symbols_named) so batched lookups do not drop mixed-case callees.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark chain over the large indexed graph (144959-caller corpus) before/after. After: fewer SQL statements executed (assert via counter), lower wall time at depth>=2, identical node/edge sets to the per-node path.

title: FRONTIER: index<->query invertibility invariant (inverse-Jacobian round-trip guarantee)
description: Generalization of Issue #12 (data indexed at count 144959 but 0 retrievable). Framing via the inverse-Jacobian idea: the index transform T maps source symbols/callers/imports into stored keys; retrieval is T^-1. Issue #12 is exactly a point where T^-1 fails to recover what T stored (non-invertible on mixed-case input). Enforce an invariant: for every entity written by the indexer there exists a query in its mode (defs/callers/imports) that returns it. Encode as a property test that fuzzes symbol casing/unicode/language and asserts write-set == retrievable-set.
design: Theoretical closure of Issue #12: assert the round-trip law (index then query = identity on the key set) instead of patching one casing bug. Share the normalization chokepoint fixed in powt. Generalizes the parity oracle (55hl) from fixed fixtures to generated inputs. Any future normalization divergence breaks this test.
acceptance_criteria: A property-based test generates symbols across casings (lower/UPPER/camel/snake), scripts (ASCII + non-ASCII), and languages; indexes them; asserts every written symbol/caller/import is retrievable via its query mode with matching counts. Fails on pre-powt main, passes after normalization is fixed. Runs in CI as the permanent anti-regression gate for the whole class.

design: semantic_chunk.rs:72-87 strips # as a comment marker universally. Introduce a per-language comment-prefix table; only treat # as a line comment for languages where it is one. Guard against attribute/# sigil pollution.
acceptance_criteria: Rust attributes (#[derive(...)]) and TS/JS private fields (#foo) are no longer treated as doc comments and no longer injected into embedding chunk text. strip_comment_marker uses a language-aware marker set (# only for Python/Ruby/Shell/etc). title: Group macOS release build onto one runner to cut CI cost (~40%)
description:
Goal: cut per-release CI cost ~40% by building BOTH macOS arches (aarch64-apple-darwin + x86_64-apple-darwin) on ONE macos-14 runner instead of two. macOS is billed 10x, so merging the two darwin jobs is the dominant saving. No cross-compilation needed.

VALIDATED: pi-cross-smoke.yml run 29979297456 built both darwin arches on one macos-14 runner and ran 'asgrep version'/'doctor' on arm64 + confirmed x64 Mach-O (5m1s). PASS.

SCOPE DECISION (user): group macOS ONLY. Keep native: linux-x64-gnu (ubuntu-latest), linux-arm64-gnu (ubuntu-24.04-arm, 1x), win32-x64-msvc (windows-latest). Do NOT adopt cross-compile: cargo-xwin for win32 is fragile (ring needs llvm-lib archiver, and cross-MSVC of a crypto crate is brittle across dep bumps); cargo-zigbuild for linux-arm64 saves ~nothing since ARM runner is 1x.

REQUIRED CHANGES:
1) Matrix data: represent darwin as ONE grouped matrix entry {id: darwin, runner: macos-14, targets: [darwin-arm64, darwin-x64], rustTargets: [aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin]} plus 3 single entries (linux-x64, linux-arm64, win32). Update packages/pi/scripts/release-artifact.mjs 'matrix' output + packages/pi/release/targets.json.
2) release-artifact.mjs prepare/verify/pack are per-target 1:1 with platform package today. Rework so one grouped build job produces BOTH darwin platform artifacts (loop over the entry's arches; prepare/verify each platform dir; still emit 5 platform packages total).
3) Workflows: pi-native-artifacts.yml (dry-run) and pi-npm-release.yml build job must loop over an entry's arches for build+prepare+pack+upload. verify-release download pattern '*' already handles multiple artifacts.
4) Harness check-native-workflow.mjs: build assertion (build.strategy.matrix===matrix && runs-on===matrix.runner) still holds since matrix still drives runs-on. Keep required step-name substrings ('cargo build --locked --release', metadata prepare/verify, all npm pack cmds, clean-install, ci-install-smoke). Keep 'matrix: {}' mutation rejected and linux-arm64 native-ARM-runner assertion. Preserve manual-only + all security invariants (SSH tag verify, protected npm-production env, id-token OIDC, provenance attestation, publish order native->launcher->extension, bootstrap-token expr).

VALIDATION (all local, $0) BEFORE any Actions run: npm run release:preflight; npm run check:pi-contract; npm run check:pi-release; launcher + extension tests; release-acceptance self-test. Optionally one manual dispatch of pi-native-artifacts.yml (dry-run) before a real release.

ACCEPTANCE: harness green with all negative mutations rejected; a real release still yields 5 platform packages + launcher (ast-sgrep) + extension (pi-ast-sgrep), with macOS built on a single runner.

NON-GOAL: not part of failure-recovery (already done: idempotent publish #1, durable GH Release assets #2, local preflight #4). This is a pure cost optimization for the (infrequent) full build.

CONTEXT: pi-cross-smoke.yml remains in-repo as a manual validation tool (win32 xwin step currently fails on missing llvm-lib; not needed for macOS-only scope).

title: Release-time + local gate enforcement (CI stays manual-dispatch by design)
description: omega-math pass-4 #82/#83, REFRAMED per owner decision: manual-dispatch CI is deliberate — no per-push workflows, GitHub Actions budget is conserved; runs happen at releases only. The surviving defects: (a) speed.yml/bakeoff.yml are test -f stubs — even when run manually at release they enforce nothing; make them actually execute the benchmark harness and fail on threshold breach so the RELEASE gate is real. (b) fuzz matrix runs parsed_query + query_grammar which are byte-identical harnesses while rank.rs (the only target with real invariants: score bounds, RRF finiteness, permutation invariance) never runs — swap one duplicate for rank; cache cargo-fuzz to save the job budget. (c) For pre-release confidence without Actions spend: add a local gate (justfile/make target or pre-push hook, e.g. cargo test --workspace + clippy + rank fuzz 30s) documented in CONTRIBUTING; release-acceptance script should invoke the same gate. Thresholds become enforceable at the two points that matter (local + release) with zero per-push cost.
close_reason: Replaced speed and bakeoff documentation stubs with real manually dispatched benchmark gates that enforce result identity, correctness, and measured latency. Added a shared local and official release gate, replaced duplicate parser fuzzing with ranking invariants, and cached cargo-fuzz. Targeted RCH evidence passed both benchmark suites, CLI contracts, clippy, and a bounded rank fuzz run. Release workflow mutation checks and gate self-test passed. Commit 038fc8c pushed to pull request 21.

title: F-09: OllamaEmbedder::dim() and CloudEmbedder::dim() return 0 (P2)
description: embedder.rs:172-175,196-199 return 0. allocators and pre-embed validators get 0 and may produce zero/empty vectors. Hidden by post-embed length detection. Fix: probe and cache, or assert at first embed. No code change.
design: embedder.rs:172-175,196-199 return 0. Probe dimension on first embed and cache in the struct (OnceCell), or assert non-zero at first embed. Currently masked by post-embed length detection; make it explicit to prevent zero/empty vector allocation.
acceptance_criteria: OllamaEmbedder::dim() and CloudEmbedder::dim() return the true embedding dimension (probed once and cached) rather than 0. Allocators and pre-embed validators receive correct dims. Test: dim() matches the length of an actual produced vector for each backend (mockable).
close_reason: OllamaEmbedder and CloudEmbedder now cache the first successful non-empty embedding response dimension in AtomicUsize; dim() returns the cached value and documents returning 0 before first success. No constructor network probe.

title: Def/Caller channel ceiling reintroduces term-count dilution for partial-coverage matches
description: e2hc.14 review P2 finding: channel_ceiling for Def/Caller scales with substantive_terms (ALL non-empty query terms) while coverage_symbol_score (rank.rs:77-79) sums only MATCHING terms and documents 'unmatched query context must not dilute evidence.' Normalization by total-term ceiling reintroduces the dilution: a partial-coverage match (1 of 3 terms exact) normalizes to ~13/33=0.39, and adding noise terms lowers it further. Unlike the Asgrep bug (ceiling unreachable, perfect match capped at 1/terms), the Def/Caller ceiling IS reachable (perfect all-terms match = 1.0), so this is milder. Fix: normalize by matched-term count or compute ceiling from per-hit achievable max, not total query term count. Found by worker review subagent on PR #22.
close_reason: Resolved in commit 945bec3 on PR 22. Def and Caller ceilings now use per-hit matched-term counts. Five targeted intent tests and clippy passed on Spark. Independent second review passed.

title: F-12: body_structure_hash treats * as trivia universally (P3)
description: index.rs:395-410 trivia check includes line.starts_with(*). Breaks Go *Type pointers and *Rust raw-deref lines. Causes refresh_lines_only false-positive → stale symbols/callers/imports. Fix: only inside open block comment, or language-aware. No code change.
design: index.rs:395-410 trivia check includes line.starts_with('*') to skip block-comment continuation. Restrict to lines inside an open block comment, or make language-aware. False positives cause stale graph rows after edits.
acceptance_criteria: body_structure_hash no longer treats a leading * as trivia universally: Go *Type and Rust raw-deref/pointer lines are not misclassified, preventing false-positive refresh_lines_only that leaves stale symbols/callers/imports. Test: a Go file with *Type line changing body triggers full re-extraction.
close_reason: Tracked block-comment state in body_structure_hash so * code remains structural; added pointer/block-comment tests.

title: F-03: symbols_named case-sensitive vs calls_matching case-insensitive (P1)
description: symbols_named (store/sqlite.rs:762-769) WHERE s.name=?1 (case-sensitive). calls_matching uses lower()=lower(). In chain.rs:111-116, callee strings from outgoing_calls feed symbols_named — case mismatch silently drops chain nodes. Fix: case-insensitive in symbols_named. No code change.
design: store/sqlite.rs:762-769 uses WHERE s.name=?1. Change to lower(s.name)=lower(?1). Confirm an index on lower(name) or accept scan cost; measure on large fixture. Sibling of powt (same case-normalization class).
acceptance_criteria: symbols_named matches case-insensitively (lower()=lower()) consistent with calls_matching. chain.rs nodes whose callee case differs from the stored symbol name are no longer silently dropped. Test: fixture with camelCase caller feeding into symbols_named returns the node.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #14/#15/#16/#17. See PR for details + regression tests. Verified on spark (cargo test + clippy).

title: NL-question retrieval eval + beat QMD as recall backend (capn-hook gap)
description: capn-hook's recall backend is QMD (github.com/tobi/qmd): semantic hybrid by default, ~300MB-2GB model download, cold ask takes seconds; BM25 fallback deterministic. Their measured retrieval: recall@k 60/60 but precision@1 only 56/60 on a 60-doc corpus — weak top-ranking at trivial scale. ast-sgrep opportunity: (1) build a natural-language-dev-question -> ground-truth-files eval corpus in their style (pinned OSS repos, hand-verified answers, precision@1 + recall@k + paraphrase robustness — the axis their eval explicitly skips); (2) benchmark ast-sgrep hybrid retrieval on it vs QMD BM25 and QMD hybrid as named competitors (bake-off culture: published losses included); (3) target: match or beat QMD hybrid precision@1 with zero model download and sub-second cold ask. Feeds wlp-embedder-quality-8370 (real local embeddings) — this corpus becomes its gate. Also positions ast-sgrep as the drop-in recall backend for any capn-style chart layer (see fszero-afo).
